fields.disappearance: 1534 CE, it is said (the record's other text gives his reign as 1497-1541)
fields.notes:
Independent Gajapati king of Orissa (reigned 1497-1541). Son of Puruṣottama Deva and Padmāvatī. Disciple of Kāśī Miśra; of the sub-branch of Gadādhara Paṇḍita (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.135; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Sons: Puruṣottama Jānā, Kaluyā Deva, Kakhāru Deva; daughter: Tukkā. The Lord refused to see a king, and embraced him at the Ratha-yātrā when he recited the Gopī-gīta (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 14). Kavi Karṇapūra wrote the Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka at his request.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: King Indradyumna, who began the worship of Jagannātha (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 118).

Boyhood friend of Nimāi in Navadvīpa and one of the most intimate associates of Lord Caitanya, «the very life of the Lord» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.21). He served the Lord in Purī; his love showed itself as anger and sulking (the pot of oil, Antya 12; Sanātana's saffron cloth, Antya 13).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: a manifestation of Satyabhāmā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 51).

fields.aka: Junior Haridāsa, Choto Haridāsa, Chota Haridasa
fields.place: Purī; left his body at Prayāga
fields.notes: Kīrtana singer of Lord Caitanya in Purī, with a very sweet voice: «Baḍa Haridāsa and Choṭa Haridāsa, two kīrtana singers» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.147). For begging rice from Mādhavī Devī the Lord gave him up; after a year he gave up his life at Prayāga and went on singing for the Lord unseen (Antya 2.100-165). Not Laghu Haridāsa.

He was the brother of Śikhi Māhiti and Mādhavī Devī, Karan by caste, and belonged to the  branch of Śrī Caitanya. According to Caitanya Caritāmṛta. 2.10.42-44, it was Sārvabhauma  who introduced Murāri to Lord Caitanya. Kavikarṇapūr in his Caitanya Caritamrtamahakavya mentions the name of Murāri Māhiti which indicates that Murāri was  a contemporary of Karṇapūra. (Bhakti Movement in Orissa  p. 84-86)

With his sister Mādhavī he accepted Lord Caitanya at once, while their brother Śikhi doubted; they stopped seeing Śikhi until his dream of the Lord merging with Jagannātha, and then the three surrendered together at the Garuḍa-stambha (Caitanya-carita-mahākāvya 13; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, entry «Śikhi Māhiti»).

He belonged to the lineage of Lord Caitanya. He constituted a Kāla (usually applied to 1/16th part of the moon) of Lord Gaurāṅga (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 74). Bhagavān was a lame resident of Halisahara. (Caitanya Caritāmṛta 1.10.136, 3.14.90,31, 2.84-85, 3.2.94- 100, 101-167, 3.5.91-158, and Sakhinirnayamrita 38)

He lived in Purī near the Lord and was a close friend of Svarūpa Dāmodara. His brother Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya came from Kāśī full of Māyāvāda Vedānta, and Svarūpa refused to hear him (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 2.85-100). He invited the Lord to his house and sent Choṭa Haridāsa to Mādhavī Devī for fine rice (Antya 2.101-167). He brought a Bengali poet's drama to be heard, and Svarūpa found its faults (Antya 5.91-158). The Abhidhāna names a Raghunātha, «son of the lame Bhagavān».
